scores.notes:
Strongest textual merge mechanics: P0-A lands every hook, signal, tunable (with end markers) and all 15 enemy moves, so UIDs are fixed early. It adds .gitattributes keep-ours for default.json, per-package act and notes files, and a resumable workflow-build.js where done means the final commit is on the branch. Its code claims mostly check out: armor hook placement before _cancel_move (combat_actor.gd:404-418), both literal &"held" plays (:477, :956), the lunge range needing widening (move_data.gd 0-4), test_tuning_panel.gd:390, test_audio.gd:175, and the 30 M2 worktrees to prune.

Problems:
(1) The grab contract has a bug. The player's safety net releases when the holder is 'not GRABBING', but EnemyHold starts the headbutt or slam with start_move(windup=false), which puts the holder in ATTACK. The player is released about 20 frames before the code-applied hit, which then lands on a free player wherever they stand.
(2) The rear-warning defaults follow_turn and drop_in_view are both true. That departs from SPEC §8 ('ends when the attack lands or is interrupted') and from the §8 default Game-boy saw.
(3) There is no readability check until all 10 phase-1 packages exist. Archetypes are tuned against P0-C's naive brain and director, which WP-AI, WP-DIR and WP-ROOM then rewrite, so that work is done twice.
(4) About 60 signatures are frozen before any code exists, which leans heavily on the amendment protocol.
(5) Six concurrent Godot-bound builders on an 8 GB machine.
(6) P0-D's crowd_bot needs P0-C's crowd room, but both are built in the same parallel wave.
(7) dummy_jab reach_m stays 0, so training-room warnings fire only within 1.0 m. KO-view suppression of the warning isn't specified.
(8) The Thug's third swing is a KNOCKDOWN ending a 30-damage chain, a contestable reading of the 15% rule.

Good ideas to keep: reach_m includes travel, no enemy FINISHER moves, over-head bars skip the boss, INT-1's magnetism-in-crowd list, the 'belly slab' knockdown-view risk, test_m3_done_when.gd with real archetypes plus check_m3_log, and the exported-binary smoke test.

Best process skeleton. S0 creates class_name skeletons (EnemyActor, EnemyDirector, EnemyCatalog), so later packages can use static types and test_scripts_compile.gd (which loads every script and scene under res://game) stays green. The hot-spot table gives exactly one owner per file per phase. S0 pre-cuts the ARCHITECTURE headings, so doc edits never collide. The training room stays frozen; 11 test files plus combo_bot preload it, as the plan claims (verified). The 26-.tres byte-identical check and the 'ResourceSaver omits default reach_m' claim are correct.

The Punk slice gate (lead plus a three-lens review, fixers, re-recording, then locking feel defaults) attacks the real M3 risk, readability in first person, before breadth. The warning is built on dummies in phase 1, independent of the AI. Pin order (the victim's priority is the holder's + 1) and the is_holding() safety net make the grab contract consistent. 'Compare moves by id; hit.move is the duplicate' is a sharp catch. It has the lowest cost (about 135-170% of a window) and caps builders at 4.

Weaknesses:
- Fewer quantified readability metrics: the gate is mostly judged by eye.
- No vehicle or stairwell spawn tag; SPEC §7 lists vehicles.
- The boss charge's reach_m is measured from the static strike pose, so a charge from 4-6 m behind may not warn. P2-kicker has the same issue with its free_lunge step-in.
- _keeps_pose_after_strike() rests on a wrong rationale: _pull_strike is set only on HitDetector hits (combat_actor.gd:200), never on code-applied grab hits.
- Only two new signals, so AI state and tokens must be polled.
- Over-head bars for the boss aren't handled.
- Phases are more serial: grabs wait until after the gate, heavies until phase 3.

Best acceptance layer:
- §1.2 makes the warning a pure ViewGeometry.warning_corner() with a hand-written truth table, including wrap-around and frame-independence rows. The rows check out against SPEC §8 (155/160° edge, 2.0 m range edge).
- A 72-bearing sweep test against the real HUD.
- A readability probe with R1-R15 thresholds, a live warning oracle in every crowd act and an autopilot.
- An evidence pack mapped clause by clause to the done-when, the L2 rubric and six review lenses.
- An early 1R check with six real Punks.

Design features worth keeping: COMMIT square-up, back-off retreat after attacking, track-then-lock wind-ups, armor that reads (spark, clank, ARMOR in the log), warning_reach_m() for the charge, KO suppression, and a vehicle spawn. The capture lock in git-common-dir works across worktrees.

Problems:
(1) 'Each WP appends its own ARCHITECTURE section' from five parallel branches collides at end of file. That is not a mechanical merge.
(2) WP-D appends RoomKit.add_ai_support() to test_room.gd. That adds a navmesh bake, a director and a spawner to the room preloaded by 11 test files and 3 bots, against the codemap's advice (dummy-room-ui.md:393-394, 506).
(3) No EnemyActor or EnemyDirector skeleton in phase 0 forces duck typing across packages, against 'static types everywhere'.
(4) R2 ('never two wind-ups starting together', marked hard) is not guaranteed by a grant gap. Wind-up start equals grant plus commit pause plus a variable step-in, so the test will fail or flake unless the gap is enforced at wind-up start.
(5) boss_slam as a FINISHER tier fires the global slow-mo and impact frame on an enemy hit.
(6) Charge distance and kicker lunge are Tuning values, though attack numbers belong in move data.
(7) Every hit gets its own 18+ frame wind-up. That is a stricter spec reading that slows the two-hit punch and three-swing combos.
(8) WP-I's probe is a large, intricate build for a Sonnet builder.

synthesis:
Start from vertical-slice. Keep its S0 → P1 (ai, director, room, hud) → P1-int → slice gate → P2 (grab, kicker, thug) → P3 (bruiser, boss) → P4 shape, its hot-spot ownership table, its S0 class_name skeletons, its pre-cut ARCHITECTURE headings and its frozen training room. Then graft and fix as follows.

**Grafts from readability-first:**
1. **S0, first commit:** a static `ViewGeometry` helper (bearing, is_outside_view, and the pure `warning_corner()`) with RF §1.2's hand-written truth table as `test_view_geometry.gd`. The player look API can wrap it. RearWarning and the director both call it.
2. **S0, tunables:** declare every known tunable now, using RF Appendix A plus VS per-package lists, so phase appends are rare.
   - Set `dummy_jab.reach_m = 1.05` in gen_moves and drop VS's `rear_warning_fallback_reach_m`.
   - Add RF's `tests/helpers/stub_ai_enemy.gd` and `stub_director.gd` as fixtures for P1-director and P1-hud.
3. **P1-hud:**
   - RF's `test_warning_sweep_every_5_degrees` (72/72) and `WARN-CHECK ok|FAIL` log lines.
   - KO suppression.
   - Reach read through an optional `attacker.warning_reach_m(move)`; the boss overrides it to add the charge distance.
   - Keep the side fixed at wind-up start, with `follow_turn` off by default.
4. **Add a fifth phase-1 package, P1-instruments** (RF WP-I: crowd_bot acts, readability probe, autopilot, warning oracle), or fold it into P1-room if headroom is tight.
   - Gate the slice on RF's hard metrics R1, R3, R10 and R11, and judge R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R12, R13 and R15 as soft metrics.
   - Redefine R2 either as a soft metric or as enforced at wind-up start: the enemy asks `director.may_start_windup()`, which applies the gap. A grant gap alone does not guarantee it.
5. **P1-ai behaviour:** RF's COMMIT square-up (`commit_pause_frames`), the RECOVER back-off to the ring, track-then-lock (`windup_track_share`) and open-handed taunts.
6. **P1-room:** add a `vehicle` spawn tag behind the parked car.
7. **P3-bruiser:** armor presentation (grey spark, clank pool, "ARMOR" in the combat log and in `HitInfo.describe()`). Give it single-phase ownership of vfx_director.gd, combat_log_overlay.gd and audio_director.gd.
8. **Gate and final review:** use RF's evidence-pack table (§1.4), the L2 rubric and lenses L1-L6, and quote `readability.json` in the PR and the digest.

**Grafts from contracts-first:**
1. **Before S0:** prune the 30 `.worktrees/m2-*` worktrees. Add `.gitattributes tuning/default.json merge=keep-ours` with `git config merge.keep-ours.driver true`, and regenerate the preset after every merge.
2. **S0 contract text:** use CF §4.3 and §4.4's exact code for the CombatActor hooks and the look API (correct placements, verified), with the fixes listed under all-missed below. Add `EnemyMoveIds` (OPENERS, CHAINS, GRAB_HITS) for dispatch and the move tests.
3. **reach_m:** document it as including the move's travel. Widen `lunge` to 0-8, or keep VS's free_lunge but measure reach including travel, so the Kicker's step-in and the boss charge's warning are right.
4. **Resumable runner:** `docs/reviews/M3/workflow-build.js` with saved args (a package is done when its final commit is on the branch, wip when the branch exists), so a usage cut-off resumes by rerunning the same args.
5. **P4-int:** CF's INT-2 `test_m3_done_when.gd` (real Punk, Kicker and Bruiser at L, R and 180°, negative controls, a 1500-frame soak) plus `check_m3_log`. Add CF's INT-1 magnetism-in-crowd list (skip get-up i-frame bodies, stop distance plus target radius, flat cone for bodies over 2 m, stomp only when no standing enemy is in the cone). P2-grab owns player.gd for this.
6. **WP-WARN items:** over-head bars skip group "boss"; the boss bar hides on `vanished`.
7. **The 'belly slab' risk:** the non-KO knockdown view covers the screen for about 1.3 s and will recur in crowds. Make it an explicit crowd-lens item.
8. **Ship step:** smoke-test the exported binary with `--quit-after 900`, publish with `gh release --prerelease`, and fix CLAUDE.md's stale '6 s'.
9. **Keep these CF decisions:** no FINISHER-tier enemy moves (so boss_slam is HEAVY/THROWN), and one telegraph per attack, with chain links allowed only after the opener landed or was blocked (RF's condition). Log the latter as a README departure.

**Fixes to vertical-slice itself:**
1. Drop `_keeps_pose_after_strike()` unless the headbutt uses a hitbox: code-applied hits never set `_pull_strike`.
2. Specify the boss charge's reach and the Kicker's lunge in reach_m.
3. Cap concurrent Godot-bound builders at 3-4.

**Requirements all three missed:**
1. **F1/F4 doesn't pause the fight.** Opening F1 or F4 only makes the player's input scripted (`tuning_overlay.gd:218-225 _freeze_player`); the game keeps running. With M3's AI and waves, the player gets beaten while Game-boy tunes live (SPEC §11). The director must grant no tokens, waves must hold and brains must idle while the overlay is open. Expose it through a sim-readable input-layer flag such as `GameInput.menu_open`, not a UI read.
2. **The mash's push is dead.** `break_free(push)` in all three plans calls `release_from_grab(push, false)`, which ignores `push` (only the stagger branch uses it, `combat_actor.gd:487-503`). Set `sim_velocity` after the release.
3. **New move fields aren't F1-editable as placed.** `reach_m` (and RF's `windup_floor`) must be declared inside a `Tuning.MOVE_GROUPS` group (`tuning.gd:45`: Movement, or Frames) to be F1-editable and saved in presets. CF and VS claim per-move F1 tuning without this.
4. **Absorbed armor hits still freeze the armored enemy.** They pass through HitDetector's hitstop (`hit_detector.gd:76-77`), so every jab lengthens a Bruiser or boss wind-up and its warning. Decide whether absorbed hits skip victim hitstop, and test it.
5. **Landed enemy strikes snap to idle after hitstop** (`_pull_strike`, `combat_actor.gd:200` and `:636-640`), so pipe, smash and pound follow-throughs vanish in first person. Add a first-person lens-clearance test for big-body strikes (2.05 m and 2.3 m rigs), not only for grabs.
6. **The usage watcher can't reach agents inside a running Workflow.** Builders need timed `wip:` commits and a resumable runner (only CF specifies one), and the lead must re-verify the watcher and the scheduled resume task at each phase boundary.
missed_requirements: Opening F1/F4 doesn't pause the fight: TuningOverlay._freeze_player() (tuning_overlay.gd:218-225) only scripts the player's input, so with M3 AI and waves the player gets beaten while Game-boy tunes live (SPEC §11). The director must grant no tokens, waves must hold and AI must idle while the overlay is open.
break_free(push) in all three plans calls release_from_grab(push, false), which ignores push (only the stagger branch uses it, combat_actor.gd:487-503), so grab_break_push_mps would do nothing.

New MoveData fields (reach_m, RF's windup_floor) must sit inside a Tuning.MOVE_GROUPS group (tuning.gd:45) to be F1-editable and saved in presets; CF and VS claim per-move F1 tuning without saying so.
Armor-absorbed hits still apply victim hitstop through HitDetector (hit_detector.gd:76-77), lengthening Bruiser and boss wind-ups and their rear warnings with every jab. Undecided and untested.

_pull_strike (combat_actor.gd:200, 636-640) snaps every enemy strike that lands on the player to idle after hitstop, so heavy follow-throughs vanish in first person. No first-person lens-clearance test for 2.05 m and 2.3 m bodies' strikes, only for grabs.

The usage watcher messages only the lead session, so agents inside a running Workflow can't be halted mid-run. Only contracts-first specifies a resumable build runner keyed on branch commit state, and none re-verifies the watcher and the scheduled resume task at phase boundaries.
